scope: ANALYSIS ONLY — not implemented. Generated from the live catalog, the graph projection and ATLAS_v2.json.

other_facts: Fasteners is a RESEARCHED formula (item.studyRecipe = fasteners); Machine Parts is known from the start. Removing the recipe deletes one research step from the Workbench III and motorbike routes.
Fasteners also arrive without crafting: creature drop from orc_3 and authored industrial loot. A merge has to convert or strand those stacks.
door_powered consumer is listed but not buildable today (module pending) and is excluded from the totals.
conclusion: M1 (n Fasteners → ceil(n/2) Machine Parts) is NOT cost-neutral for a single consumer. Total iron is about unchanged (12.999 → 13) but scrap rises on every row: best case 1.5×, worst case 3× (the 12 one-fastener consumers). Across all 22 live consumers scrap goes 12.999 → 26.

M2 (write the batch ratio into the consumer: ceil(n/3) ingot + ceil(n/3) scrap) costs exactly what one fastener batch costs today for an isolated craft, but removes leftover sharing: pooled cost rises up to 3× on one-fastener consumers (12.999 → 24 scrap overall).
No integer mapping removes Fasteners without a cost jump on the one- and two-fastener consumers. That is the blocker; it is arithmetic, not taste.
resolution: RULING APPLIED: Fasteners stay. The Round 1 disposition MERGE_CANDIDATE is withdrawn (now KEEP).

If the twin signal is to be removed later, do it by DIFFERENTIATION, not by merge: Fasteners = researched joining stock for assemblies and field repair; Machine Parts = base mechanism stock. That needs no recipe change.

A future merge is only admissible with a replacement that is priced per consumer in thirds (i.e. keeps a 3-per-batch unit) — which is Fasteners under another name. Close P2 unless a new mechanic is proposed.

conclusion: MEASURED BLOCKER: a player cannot obtain the 240 HP Plank Wall in the live build. It is upgrade-only geometry (buildReason refuses to place it), and no entry of STRUCTURE_UPGRADES leads to it (wall_wood upgrades straight to wall_stone). The "240 HP wall route" the question asks about does not exist at this base.
The same test finds every structure in that state: wall_plank (240 HP), wall_brick (600 HP). The Brick Wall is affected exactly like the Plank Wall.

Consequence: Plank has 1 listed consumer (structure:wall_plank) and zero REACHABLE consumers. It is craftable (6s at a Workbench) and drops from orc_2, but nothing a player can do spends it. The Round 1 projection counted the structure cost as a consumer; that was an over-count.

If the tier were reachable, removing the Workbench step would leave the wood bill unchanged (11 wood cumulative) and save 18s of bench time per wall plus the one-time Workbench. HP per wood: Wood Wall 32, Plank Wall cumulative 21.818 — the plank tier is LESS wood-efficient than the wood wall, so the bench step is not what protects the wood tier.
resolution: RULING APPLIED: Plank stays; nothing is retired. The Round 1 disposition RETIRE_CANDIDATE is withdrawn (now DEFER, flagged NO_REACHABLE_CONSUMER).

Option A — intermediate tier: route wall_wood → wall_plank → wall_stone. Measured side effect: the Stone Wall route gains one upgrade step (+6 wood, +18s) unless STRUCTURE_UPGRADES is taught to branch. That is a cost change on a live route and needs approval.

Option B — move the processing step: let a placed Wood Wall be upgraded to Plank Wall as an OPTIONAL side branch (map becomes one-to-many), Stone route untouched. No existing cost moves; this is the cheapest way to make Plank live.
Option C — retire the Plank Wall tier and the item together. Rejected for this round by the ruling.
Recommended next action: decide A or B in the building ontology PR (#56 line), because the upgrade map lives there; then re-run this section — it will flip to "obtainable" on its own.

conclusion: No Veyra source at all (6 of 8): chitin, crawler_optic, wolf_fang, beetle_horn, keycard, core_demon.

Cause, by item. Dropped only by creatures behind the Shipping spawner: chitin, crawler_optic, wolf_fang, beetle_horn. Held only in authored Shipping/Dev containers: keycard, core_demon. The creatures and crates exist; the Veyra layout has no placement for them.

Veyra-blocked recipes and the input that blocks each: chitin_armor (needs chitin); core_demon (needs crawler_optic); essence_spirit (needs crawler_optic); pump_crude (needs a blocked input); refinery_crude (needs crude_petroleum).

Reachable on Veyra by drop but not by craft: essence_spirit (CREATURE_DROP creature:boss_custodian [gate:veyra_spawner]; CREATURE_DROP creature:vampire_3 p=0.35 [gate:veyra_spawner]). For these the recipe is dead weight on Veyra while the item itself is obtainable.
Has a Veyra source: boar_tusk.

Specimens also carry a research route (crawler_optic → gas_mask; wolf_fang → fur_cloak; beetle_horn → chitin_armor; boar_tusk → iron_sword): without the specimen the formula can only come from a blueprint or paid study.
resolution: No source was invented. The matrix is the work order for the Veyra content pass: per NO_VEYRA_SOURCE item choose (a) a Veyra spawner entry for the dropping creature, (b) an authored Veyra crate, or (c) an explicit "Shipping-only by design" ruling.

Until that pass: hide the Veyra-blocked recipes from the Veyra craft list using `veyra_blocked_recipes` (display filter; no recipe or save change). NOT implemented this round — it changes what a Veyra player sees and was not in the authorised set.

Keycard — ROUND 3, measured: the Veyra layouts have 0 keycard doors (graph.summary.veyraPoiStats.keycardDoors, pinned in item-ontology-v2.test.ts), so "no source" is correct by design. No Keycard is added.

conclusion: Crude Petroleum stays FIXTURE_ONLY: the only oil source the engine accepts is one registered by the test fixture (registerTestOilSource), so pump_crude and refinery_crude cannot run on either live layout.

UI rule: no player-facing text may describe Crude Petroleum as something that can be pumped today. The item description and the Oil Pump description are quoted above so the wording can be reviewed against that rule.
resolution: Keep the id, the pump and the recipes (the oil-mobility work depends on them). No removal.

Display fix to schedule with the pump work, not here: mark the two recipes and the Oil Pump as "no oil seep on this map" when the layout has no authored source, instead of offering a machine that can never start. Salvaged Oil → Fuel Can at the Furnace remains the one live fuel route.

conclusion: The two families are different mechanics, not duplicates: a legacy core is a single-effect CHARGE tool (Stack.charge, 3–4 casts, re-charged as an item), a Creator Core is a three-ability RESERVE weapon (Stack.reserves) fed by the Energy/Essence economy.

Two legacy effects have no Creator counterpart: Quake Core breaks rock into yield (harvest), Rime Core makes shallow water walkable (traversal). Ember and Storm overlap a Creator ability (fireball; lightning) but keep one distinct rule each (ignites vegetation; stronger in rain).

The legacy cores are load-bearing for the Creator Cores themselves: CREATOR_LOOT_V1 finds the crate that holds a Creator Core by the legacy core in it (factory_vault/core_fire → core_dragon; light_top/core_storm → core_meteor; wreck/core_frost → core_elsa). Removing the legacy items from those crates silently removes three Creator Core sources.

Cost check: legacy cores cost 8–10 Parts at a level-1 Workbench but are tier-3 knowledge; the two common Creator Cores cost 4 Parts and are known from the start. The legacy four are not a cheaper path into the Creator line.
The one real defect is presentation: all eleven use the same gold Core frame and the same "CORE" class, so a newcomer reads eleven Cores where the Bible names seven.
resolution: PROPOSED CANON DECISION (one, concrete): keep all four as a named minor class — "Field Core" / VN "Lõi dã chiến" — single-effect charge tools, explicitly NOT among the seven Creator Cores. Bible §Creator Cores gains one sentence saying so.

What that implies when approved (nothing done now): class chip FIELD CORE instead of CORE; the gold frame and Creator VFX grammar reserved for the seven; no recipe, charge, loot or save change; ids unchanged.
What it rules out: retiring the four recipes or stripping the items from crates. Both lose unique effects and the second breaks Creator Core loot lookup.
Owner input still required: the name ("Field Core") and whether Ember/Storm should be re-tuned so they stop echoing Meteor/Mjolnir. Until then P10 is OPEN.

conclusion: The atlas file in this repository (web/ref/atlas/extracted/ATLAS_v2.json) yields 86 unique item ids: 51 recipe outputs, 30 ingredient ids, 36 loot items and 20 entries in its items block, de-duplicated (48 ids appear in more than one of those places).

RESOLVED 2026-11-14: the 137-entry source was delivered (LI_137_ITEM_HISTORICAL_ATLAS_AUDIT.csv, SHA-256 e4a1b066…70c5). It is 137 distinct historical item ids: 84 ATLAS_INDEXED + 45 EXTERNAL_CRAFT_OR_INPUT + 8 OFFICIAL_MODERN. The earlier reading "86 ids + 51 recipe entries = 137" was a coincidence and is withdrawn. 84 ids are shared with this atlas, 53 are historical-only and 2 atlas ids are absent from the historical set.

The row-by-row comparison is in web/ref/item-ontology-v2/LI_HISTORICAL_CROSSWALK.md and li-historical-crosswalk.csv (one decision per id, provenance grade, alias / version relation, gameplay-role status).

Inside the 86: 12 ids rest only on unconfirmed evidence (recipe confidence below B, or loot edges that are not "confirmed"), 4 are named only as an ingredient with no source recorded, 0 have more than one recipe entry, and 2 stems have tier/material variants.
resolution: No Last Island item was added to SOH on the strength of this comparison. Firearms, ammunition and explosives stay out of scope.

The 137 historical ids are multi-version evidence, not a parity target. Two design candidates were recorded for their owners (an additional head-armour tier; a pedalled vehicle whose cost is breath and then HP). Neither is approved and neither was added. 15 historical rows have no supporting source and 23 rest on pages that were not re-read; see the source-support columns.
